schema.note: An episode is an ordered list of beats. Beats block: each one finishes before the next starts, because a scripted scene whose steps overlap is a race, not a scene. This file is shaped for UnityEngine.JsonUtility, which is why 'Kind' is an integer and not a string -- JsonUtility deserialises enums from numbers only. 'KindName' and 'Note' sit beside them for humans and are ignored by the parser. Do not delete the integers.

beatKinds.1: FadeOut   -- cover the screen. Seconds is the fade length.
beatKinds.2: FadeIn    -- reveal. Seconds is the fade length.
beatKinds.4: Dialogue  -- play the sequence named by Id from dialogue.json, block until it ends. Target='starter' means: suffix Id with '_' + the chosen starter's game species id, so one beat can resolve to one of three authored sequences.
beatKinds.5: TakeControl -- freeze the player, flow to Cutscene.
beatKinds.7: MoveActor -- walk the actor named by Id to the marker named by Target, block until it arrives. The actor faces the player on arrival. Seconds is a timeout, not a duration: if the walk has not finished by then, snap and continue, so blocked geometry can never strand the scene.
beatKinds.8: CameraTo  -- frame the camera on the marker named by Id (OverworldCameraRig.LookToward). Markers are listed in cast.json.
beatKinds.9: ChooseStarter -- open the starter choice, block until the player commits. StarterSelection.Commit runs InitialiseNewGame, so this beat is the point of no return.
beatKinds.10: GiveItem -- Id is a FieldItems id, Amount is the count.
beatKinds.11: SetFlag  -- Id is the flag, Value is on/off. Flags gate episodes, NPC dialogue variants and the gate ramp.
beatKinds.12: Battle   -- Id is a trainer id. The runner hands off to that trainer's TrainerController and blocks until NotifyBattleResolved. Target='starter_counter' means the party is built from StarterOption.RivalCounterSpeciesId rather than from the TrainerDefinition's fixed list.
beatKinds.13: AskName  -- NEW. Opens name entry, blocks, writes PlayerProfile.SetTrainerName. Id is the default used if the player confirms an empty field or the UI does not exist yet. Target names the profile field.

episodeFields.CompletionFlag: set when the episode ends; an episode with its flag set never replays.
episodeFields.NextEpisodeId: NEW. Played immediately when this one finishes. Used only where two scenes are really one scene split for authoring.
episodeFields.Trigger: NEW, advisory. How this episode starts when it is not chained and not the auto-played opening. Nothing reads it yet; it is here so the wiring is written down next to the scene it belongs to rather than only in a scene file.

gaps: FadeIn/FadeOut, Dialogue, MoveActor and Battle are logged-and-skipped in EpisodeRunner today. Everything below assumes they land.
AskName (13) has no UI anywhere in the project. Until it does, the beat must fall through to its Id ('Ren') rather than block forever.
CameraTo resolves markers with GameObject.Find. None of the markers named here exist in the scenes yet; their world positions are in cast.json.
NPC_Professor does not exist in slice_layout.json. Every beat that names it needs that NPC placed first; position in cast.json.
Dialogue text uses a {PLAYER} token. Nothing substitutes it yet -- DialogueRunner is the natural place.

Episodes.Note: Cold open. Black screen, the professor's voice, the name, then the game's signature first frame: the lab dome filling the top of the screen from the plaza spawn. Structural model is Diamond/Pearl's title-screen Rowan monologue plus the red-Gyarados TV report, compressed into one because this game has no bedroom interior to watch a television in. Ends with control, and the rival four metres up the lab lane. Target length ~75s.

Beats.Note: Before anything. The player never has control during the prologue.
Guarantee black on the first frame rather than trusting the boot state.
Framed behind the black, so the fade-in reveals the dome already composed.
7 lines over black. Auto-advancing except the last two. ~28s.
2 lines. Uses {PLAYER}.
Slow. This is the shot the whole town was built around.
No text. Let the dome sit there.
The morning bulletin off the plaza research terminal. This is the Diamond/Pearl television report: it names the mystery and points at the lake. 3 lines, all auto-advancing, ~11s.
Free on the plaza. Kes is up the lab lane; Sela in the market row points at him if the player wanders.

Trigger.fallback: proximity 3.0m, so a player who walks past Kes without pressing anything still starts the game

Episodes.Note: The heart of it. Diamond/Pearl's structure with one documented deviation. DP: rival drags you out of town -> an adult stops you from entering the grass -> wild birds attack -> the briefcase is opened out of necessity -> you choose. All four of those survive here; only the stage moves, from Lake Verity to the head of the gate ramp, because that is where this map puts the boundary between safe and not. Target length ~3min.

Beats.Note: 4 lines, one cosmetic choice. Both options land on the same line -- DP does not let you refuse, and pretending otherwise is worse than not asking.
Kes runs. He should arrive well before the player.
Walk, not run. 9m up the main street. The camera is already looking past them both at the ramp.
Bram. This is DP's mother warning you out of the tall grass, given to the NPC the layout already stood at the gate. 5 lines.
Swing down the ramp to the route floor -- the shot the flock comes up through.
DP's two wild Starly, restaged as a scare rather than a battle. Line 0 carries EventId 'vfx.flock_startle'; the flock itself is VFX/prop work that does not exist. 5 lines.
Linden comes up the main street from the lab lane, ~11m. He is slow on purpose; the line he speaks on arrival is about being old.
9 lines. Line 7 carries EventId 'story.case_open' for the case-opening VFX and sting.
Push in. Three balls fill the frame; this is the only close shot in the episode.
1 line, then the choice opens. Deliberately short -- the player should be reading ball labels, not dialogue.
Option copy is in cast.json under starterOptions. StarterSelection.Commit fires here: party, bag and save all begin at this instant.
Resolves to op_choice_result_1 / _5 / _10 by the chosen game species id. Each is Linden's read on the one you took plus Kes announcing the one that beats it.

5 lines. Linden explicitly calls it a loan until you come to the lab -- that is DP, where the starter is only formally yours when Rowan registers it at Sandgem, and it is what gives 'leaving_town' a reason to exist.
Switches Bram from gate_block_no_starter to gate_block_no_dex.
Handed back for a beat before Kes turns round. Chained, not merged, so the opening can be played and judged on its own.

Episodes.Note: Platinum's structure, not Diamond/Pearl's. In DP the first battle is two wild Starly and Kes has no Pokemon until Route 203, several hours later; Platinum moved the starter choice to Route 201 and made the rival battle immediate. Immediate is the right call here: this slice is one town, one route, one lake, and a rival who challenges you two towns from now has nowhere to do it. The battle runs through TrainerController -- exclamation, approach, dialogue, battle -- not through a second path. Target length ~2min including the battle.

Beats.Note: TrainerController plays riv_pre before and riv_lost/riv_won after; both are on the definition in trainers.json. The party is one creature at level 5, the counter to whatever the player took.
Linden, and written to play identically whether the player won or lost -- he is commenting on the fact of the battle, not its result. 3 lines.
CONFLICT: TrainerController.ReturnToPost walks him back to the lab lane the moment the battle resolves. Either give the controller a new rest post or suppress the return for this one fight.

Episodes.Note: What gates the ramp. Three states, in this order: no Pokemon -> Bram refuses outright; Pokemon but no dex -> Bram sends you back up the hill because Linden asked him to; dex -> open. That is DP's shape (starter at the lake, but the real freedom -- the dex, the balls, permission -- comes from the lab afterwards) folded into one town. The dex handover is also where the bag gets explained: InitialiseNewGame already granted 10 balls, 5 potions and 2 antidotes at the moment of choosing, so Linden names that exact kit instead of the data and the fiction disagreeing. Target length ~60s.

Beats.Note: 8 lines. Line 1 carries EventId 'story.starter_registered', line 2 carries 'story.dex_given' for the item-get jingle and card.
The one thing actually handed over here, because the rest of the kit came with the starter. A Town Map / journal key item would be the DP-faithful gift and FieldItems has no key items at all.
2 lines. Sends the player at the ramp.
The LevelTransition at the gate ramp must test this. Nothing tests it today -- the ramp is walkable from frame one.
